source.title: One Model for All: Large Language Models are Domain-Agnostic Recommendation Systems
source.authors: Zuoli Tang; Zhaoxin Huan; Zihao Li; Xiaolu Zhang; Jun Hu; Chilin Fu; Jun Zhou; Lixin Zou; Chenliang Li

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how recommendation performance changes with pretrained language-model size, a downstream-performance question, using recommendation metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are downstream recommendation performance across model sizes. The training-loss curves in Figure 15 vary learning rate and training steps, not model size, tokens, or compute, and are not held-out pretraining-loss scaling results. The study does not measure compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or compare depth and width at a fixed parameter count.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes and zero-shot-evaluates pretrained LMs from 40M to 6.7B parameters (BERT, OPT, FLAN-T5) on sequential recommendation. It reports how Recall changes with model size, so it bears on V6 in a new downstream setting. It fits no scaling law and reports no pretraining loss. The authors argue explicitly that 'bigger is better' does not hold well for fine-tuned recommendation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. As pretrained LM size increases, fine-tuned in-domain recommendation improves only slightly, with little gain beyond about 100M. Zero-shot domain performance improves significantly. Architecture strongly affects zero-shot results. PEFT underperforms full fine-tuning for small models (<1B).
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pretrained language models for recommendation and evaluates Recall@1 or Recall@10 across model sizes. It does not fit held-out pretraining cross-entropy power laws or compute-optimal parameter/token splits.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported size-performance trend differs between fine-tuned and zero-shot settings, and between model architectures; fine-tuning method also affects recommendation performance, with LoRA gaps from full fine-tuning varying by size and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: At similar size, model family has an overwhelming effect on zero-shot recommendation: OPT is much better than FLAN-T5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture family affects downstream transfer more than parameter count within an order of magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: The gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning narrows as size grows. It closes above 1B for OPT but not for FLAN-T5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning becomes competitive only at larger scale, depending on architecture.

record.problems: The evidence is for recommendation metrics, not held-out pretraining loss. The text gives only selected summary comparisons; many per-size values are plotted rather than stated in prose. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these results, and the authors note that architecture changes zero-shot performance.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 11 and Figure 12 contain additional per-size and per-domain plotted values not individually transcribed here; the retained rows cover the size trends and exceptions explicitly summarized in the text.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss is measured across size, tokens or compute.
No power-law loss fit in another regime. The fine-tuning results concern Recall, not the fitted form of the loss.
'Predictably' is not tested: no fitted trend, and no link to pretraining loss. Size comparisons use off-the-shelf checkpoint families trained on different data and recipes.

missing.what: Per-size Recall@1 values for each domain and backbone (FPFT and PEFT). Examples: OPT Office FPFT 12.47→13.28; FLAN-T5 Scientific near 0 at 40M under PEFT.
FLAN-T5 40M–5.5B Recall@10 by item-frequency bucket. Tail-item performance improves progressively with size while head items barely change.
Item exposure by frequency bucket across FLAN-T5 sizes.

record.verdict_notes: The size series are off-the-shelf checkpoint families, not controlled scaling runs, so they bear only loosely on 'predictable' scaling. The Figure 15 loss curves vary learning rate, not scale.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating held-out pretraining loss from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count and their effect on held-out loss.
Power-law loss scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests downstream recommendation performance against model size, but not predictability from pretraining loss or performance on other downstream task families.
Fitted scaling exponents, compute-optimal split estimates, and how fitting choices change them.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot recommendation on unseen domains (Food, Home), OPT 125M–6.7B and FLAN-T5 40M–5.5B
relationships.reason: Zero-shot Recall@10 is described as greatly improved as size grows, apart from the bugged OPT-350M checkpoint (r6, r7, r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot Recall@10 improved substantially with size, except for the faulty OPT-350M checkpoint.

relationships.reason: Recall@1 rises by 10% relative for BERT and 33% relative for FLAN-T5 over this range (r1, r2).
relationships.display_finding: Recall@1 increased by 10% relative for BERT and 33% relative for FLAN-T5.

relationships.reason: Gains saturate across all three families. OPT 125M→6.7B gives a small gain, BERT-340M is not clearly better than 110M, and a tenfold FLAN-T5 increase gives 2–5% (r3, r4, r5). The authors say this differs from NLP and CV.
relationships.display_finding: OPT gained little from 125M to 6.7B, BERT-340M was not clearly better than 110M, and tenfold FLAN-T5 scaling yielded only 2–5% gains.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
